comment: each file is served in place of served/checkpoint, over the honest tiles, under trust.cbor; every one MUST be refused. `signature_blind_accepts` lists the ones whose only defect is a signature that does not verify: a reader that never calls Ed25519 accepts exactly those, and nothing else here

reasons.01-unsigned: the checkpoint body with no signature line at all: nothing vouches for this tree
reasons.02-wrong-log-key: signed under the log's own name by a key the anchor does not pin
reasons.03-wrong-origin: another log's checkpoint, signed by this network's key under that log's name: the key id is not the anchor's, so the signature refuses it before the origin line is read. Either rule alone refuses it; `10` is the origin case
reasons.04-forged-log-signature: the log's signature line is the right shape and the right key id, and does not verify
reasons.05-one-cosignature-short: one witness of the two the policy requires
reasons.06-no-cosignatures: signed by the log and cosigned by nobody
reasons.07-unnamed-witness-only: cosigned only by a witness the policy never names, which counts for nothing
reasons.08-forged-cosignature: two cosignature lines, both naming witnesses the policy lists, one of which does not verify: the quorum is met only by a verifier that does not check them
reasons.09-extension-line: a fourth body line, signed and cosigned exactly as correctly as the real one: §6 allows origin, size and root and nothing else
reasons.10-wrong-body-origin: signed by this network's log key, under this network's name, and its origin line names another log
reasons.11-forged-cosignature-with-quorum: three named witnesses, two of whose cosignatures verify: the quorum is met without the third, and §10 refuses the checkpoint anyway
reasons.12-second-line-from-one-witness: all three witnesses cosign and verify, and `friend` carries a second, newer line that does not: a reader taking each witness's newest verifying line sees a full quorum, and §10 refuses the checkpoint anyway
reasons.13-ascii-dash-signature: the log's signature line opens with an ASCII hyphen instead of §7's em dash
reasons.14-unterminated-signature-block: the last signature line does not end in a newline, so the block is unterminated
reasons.15-size-leading-zero: the size line carries a leading zero, which is not canonical decimal
reasons.16-two-log-signatures: two signature lines name the log's key and one does not verify: a reader that stops at the first valid one accepts a checkpoint carrying a forgery
reasons.17-root-wrong-length: the root line decodes to 33 bytes whose first 32 are the honest root: a reader that takes the first 32 and reads on matches the rebuilt tree and accepts it, so §6's length is the only rule that can refuse it
reasons.18-signature-name-with-space: a signature line whose name carries a space: split at the first space the payload is not base64, split at the last it is a signature from a name nobody lists, which §10 ignores rather than refuses
reasons.19-signature-unpadded-base64: the last signature line's payload is unpadded base64: the same bytes to a raw-base64 reader, and not §7's encoding
reasons.20-signature-payload-too-long: one byte appended to the log's 68-byte payload: a verifier that reads the first 68 and stops verifies it, so this head has unboundedly many byte-distinct forms that are all valid
reasons.21-origin-with-a-suffix: this network's origin plus one base32 character, signed by this network's key under this network's name and cosigned by every witness: a reader that accepts an origin line extending this network's accepts it
reasons.22-origin-in-upper-case: this network's origin with its base32 in upper case, signed by this network's key under this network's name and cosigned by every witness: a reader that folds case accepts it
reasons.23-origin-truncated: this network's origin less its last character, signed by this network's key under this network's name and cosigned by every witness: a reader that accepts an origin line this network's origin extends accepts it
reasons.24-signature-non-canonical-pad-bits: the log's signature line with a non-zero padding bit in its last data character: a decoder that ignores padding bits reads the honest 68 bytes, and this line is not their encoding
reasons.25-empty-signature-name: one more signature line whose key name is empty: a reader that reads it as a stranger's line and ignores it accepts a malformed note
reasons.26-stranger-line-wrong-length: one more signature line under a name the policy does not list, with an 80-byte payload: a reader that ignores a stranger's line whatever its length accepts a malformed note

14-unterminated-signature-block.says: including the last, ends in one

16-two-log-signatures.says: Every signature line whose name and key id match

20-signature-payload-too-long.says: The decoded payload is **exactly** that length

21-origin-with-a-suffix.says: neither an extension of it nor a truncation

23-origin-truncated.says: neither an extension of it nor a truncation
